reason: Attacked and survived, and it is now stronger than the verifier left it, because I opened a full text of the named translation rather than reasoning from the French. The University of Southern Maine Department of Theatre production script of Tartuffe, title page By Moliere, Translated By Richard Wilbur, is a complete playing text of Wilbur's translation; I downloaded the PDF and extracted it with pdftotext. Wilbur's six lines stand there character for character as proposed: Ah, Brother, man's a strangely fashioned creature / Who seldom is content to follow Nature, / But recklessly pursues his inclination / Beyond the narrow bounds of moderation, / And often, by transgressing Reason's laws, / Perverts a lofty aim or noble cause. The capitals Brother, Nature and Reason are Wilbur's, the comma after fashioned creature's clause is Wilbur's, and the line after it is A passing observation, but it applies, which is Wilbur for Que cela vous soit dit en passant, mon beau-frere. So the full stop after cause is the real stop, not a cut. The scene headings in that text put the passage inside SCENE FIVE of Act One, between the Orgon and Cleante scene heading and the Act II heading, so Act One, scene 5 is right, and the speaker is Cleante, correctly named in parentheses after the locator. The French confirms the same place independently: Acte I, scene 5, Cleante's tirade, with mon beau-frere fixing Orgon as the addressee, and the French line before the passage closes its own sentence, so Ah, Brother opens a sentence and the quotation does not start mid-clause. Wilbur's Tartuffe is 1963, Harcourt, Brace and World, which the source line has right. Attribution is clean and the misattribution list has no Moliere trap. shipped.js returns no hit, no near-hit, person jean baptiste poquelin at 0 of 3, not banned, and Moliere appears in no carry-in, so there is no twice-in-the-month collision. Tag Drama is the form of the work. Scope is clean: a play of 1669 in a 1963 translation, no scripture, no oratory, no lyric, nothing needing a warning, and counsel from one man to his brother-in-law is exactly May's theme. Verse lineation is kept with the slash convention and the translation's own capitals at each line head. The source line leads with the name, carries no dash and runs 75 characters, and it names the translator and year as rule 4 requires.

residual: Two things in the verifier's evidence are weaker than its confidence. First, the Los Angeles Review of Books article it leans on does not print the first two lines: it adapts them to man, a strangely fashioned creature, / seldom is content to follow Nature, so it never confirmed Ah, Brother or Who. The production script does, which is why this survives. Second, the claim that the French runs lines 339 to 344 in the standard numbering was not checked by me and should be dropped rather than carried, since the shipped source line does not need it. One small style point: the source line mixes Act One in words with scene 5 in a numeral.
